prompt.text: Use code 1 for a table, 2 for a bar graph, 3 for a pictogram, 4 for a line graph and 5 for a pie chart. A school's electricity comes from solar 40%, wind 30%, gas 20% and other sources 10%. A report needs one compact chart showing each share, and exact figures appear separately. For the reason code, use 1 if a bar graph cannot show percentages, 2 if a bar graph would compare the sources but not show them as parts of one whole, or 3 if a bar graph needs at least five categories. Enter a two-digit number: the first digit is the code of the most suitable display and the second digit is the reason code.

content.text: Ask whether the four sources together make up one whole.
The four percentages add up to 100%, and exact figures appear separately. Choose the display that gives a quick overview of shares of one whole, then think about what a bar graph does not show.

A pie chart shows the four sources as parts of the school's whole electricity supply in one compact chart. A bar graph would compare the sources but would not show them as parts of one whole, so the reason code is 2.
